## Why visit

A useful specialist addition to Birkenhead when you want an extensive own-brewery tasting in a production setting. The brewery advertises a large tap range and a spacious room, making it a different experience from the town’s traditional pubs. Its proximity to Gallaghers means a visit can contrast regional cask in a local with modern beer at its source. Include it for that direct brewing connection and style breadth; if every stop must serve real ale, the current evidence does not make it suitable.

## Beer

CAMRA explicitly reports no real ale; the operator advertises a large own-beer tap selection. Treat this as a keg-focused stop.

## Cider and perry

**Real-cider offering not established.** No current real-cider offering established; ask which producer and product is available.

See [how cider is classified](../real-cider.md).

## Food

Not established; do not plan a meal here without checking.

## Plan the visit

Normally Thursday–Sunday. Use the operator’s Lightbox address; CAMRA’s older listing calls it Lighthouse. Office hours are not taproom hours.

**Getting there:** Operator gives walking directions from Hamilton Square via Chester Street and past Gallaghers; Birkenhead Central is another nearby rail option.

Check [November transport issues](../logistics.md) for date-specific disruption.
